items.stem: Under absorption costing, if production exceeds sales in a period, reported profit compared with marginal costing will generally be:

options.text: Higher, because fixed overhead is carried forward in closing inventory
options.rationale: Correct: absorption costing defers fixed overhead in inventory, raising profit when inventory increases.

options.text: Lower, because fixed overhead is written off immediately
options.rationale: Writing off fixed overhead immediately is marginal costing, which gives lower profit here.

options.text: The same, because inventory valuation does not affect profit
options.rationale: Inventory valuation differs between the methods and does affect profit.
Profit is not forced to zero by the costing method.

items.explanation: Correct: absorption costing defers fixed overhead in inventory, raising profit when inventory increases.

items.stem: In short-term limiting-factor decision making, products should be ranked by:

options.text: Contribution per unit of the limiting factor
options.rationale: Correct: ranking by contribution per unit of the scarce resource maximises total contribution.
Revenue ignores variable costs and the scarce resource constraint.
Price alone ignores cost and the limiting factor.
Fixed cost per unit is not the basis for short-term ranking.

items.explanation: Correct: ranking by contribution per unit of the scarce resource maximises total contribution.

items.stem: Select TWO valid approaches to dealing with risk and uncertainty in short-term decisions.

options.text: Expected value analysis using outcome probabilities
options.rationale: Correct: expected values summarise risky outcomes by probability weighting.
Correct: these rules reflect pessimistic or optimistic attitudes to uncertainty.

options.text: Assuming the future will exactly equal last year
options.rationale: Assuming no change ignores uncertainty rather than dealing with it.

options.text: Using only sunk costs in the analysis
options.rationale: Sunk costs are irrelevant to decisions.

options.text: Deleting all unfavourable outcomes from the model
options.rationale: Removing bad outcomes distorts rather than addresses risk.

items.explanation: Correct: expected values summarise risky outcomes by probability weighting.
